extracted.intended_audience: researchers and grant writers preparing NIH grant applications (FORMS‑I)
extracted.subtask_description: A practical, step‑by‑step workbook for writing competitive NIH proposals (FORMS‑I), focusing on composing each application component, improving experimental rigor and transparency, and addressing NIH‑specific requirements and changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Packaging and presentation (grantsmanship)
rubrics_metrics.description: Good ideas submitted to the NIH are turned down more often because of poor packaging and presentation — i.e., poor grantsmanship — than for any other reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize clear, persuasive packaging of the proposal; avoid poor grantsmanship. The Workbook is designed to help avoid the trap of poor presentation by showing how to present your application effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write each component of the proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: The Workbook will serve as your step-by-step guide to writing a compelling, fundable NIH grant application. We explain how to write each component of the proposal, after which we offer an example.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each component: read the explanation, review the provided example, then write something comparable for your subject — iteratively building the first draft of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of examples and iterative drafting
rubrics_metrics.description: After explaining each component, the Workbook offers an example and invites you to write comparable content so the first draft gradually falls into place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn by modeling examples and producing immediate practice content; this iterative approach is presented as a recommended workflow for assembling a complete application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to current NIH FORMS and administrative changes
rubrics_metrics.description: This NEWLY UPDATED version (January 2026) includes information about the NIH FORMS‑I application package and other recent changes made by NIH, as well as updated URLs and screenshots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure applications follow the current FORMS‑I requirements and other NIH policy changes that affect forms, content, and submission; use up‑to‑date screenshots/URLs as procedural guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigor of experimental design
rubrics_metrics.description: This edition includes guidance on how to improve the rigor of experimental design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengthen study design elements (controls, reproducibility, appropriate methods) and explicitly address design choices that affect validity and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of the proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes guidance on how the transparency of your proposal can be enhanced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about methods, data handling, inclusion/exclusion criteria, analysis plans, and limitations to improve reviewer trust and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presenting the rigor of the scientific background
rubrics_metrics.description: Demystifies how you should present the rigor of the scientific background for your application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how prior work, preliminary data, and literature collectively support the proposed research and demonstrate an accurate, critical understanding of the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss strengths and limitations of preliminary results and published literature
rubrics_metrics.description: How you should discuss strengths and limitations of preliminary results and published literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly acknowledge limitations in preliminary data and prior studies, and explain how those limitations inform the proposed approach or interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Different uses of conceptual and technical preliminary results
rubrics_metrics.description: Different uses of conceptual and technical preliminary results are also described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between conceptual (hypothesis‑motivating) and technical (feasibility/technical proof) preliminary data and explain their appropriate role in supporting aims and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach subsection: address biological variation, especially sex
rubrics_metrics.description: The chapter on the Approach subsection of the Research Strategy was previously expanded to help you address potential sources of biological variation, especially those related to sex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the Approach, explicitly identify and plan for sources of biological variation (including sex as a biological variable), detailing experimental design, sample size/analysis adjustments, and interpretation strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance and Innovation subsections
rubrics_metrics.description: Table of Contents includes 'Significance & Innovation Subsections' as discrete topics covered by the Workbook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare clear Significance and Innovation sections that articulate the importance of the problem, gaps in knowledge, and how the proposed work is novel or transformative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior/Key Personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Table of Contents includes 'Senior/Key Personnel' as a topic in the Workbook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe qualifications, roles, and contributions of senior and key personnel, demonstrating appropriate expertise and a management plan that supports successful execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Find program / grant mechanism selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Table of Contents lists 'Find Program / Grant Mechanism' as a covered topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and justify the most appropriate NIH institute/center and grant mechanism for your project; aligning aims and scope with the selected program increases fit and competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigor of Research Design (chapter focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Workbook contains a chapter titled 'Rigor of Research Design'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat rigor as a distinct, evaluable element of the application: include methods to ensure reproducibility, mitigate bias, and validate findings; present these clearly in the Research Strategy.
